answer: A close sealed only 8,183 grader seats against 18,064 panels drawn and 16,357 rows waiting, so panel access is the scarce good. Auction it: the clearing price is the echo of the crowd's demand, last close's grading fee per sealed seat times the rows drawn per sealed seat. A row that draws no seat waits, and at TTL expiry loses its claim. One honest head bids once and is drawn anyway. A farm's tenth head meets a deeper tide of bids, so its anchor costs more than its first, and no bid splits or pre-ages.
